title: Rice Straw Tissue Preparation for Electron Microscopy Imaging
author: Mohamadiaza, Farrokhi, et al.
materials: Until now, in most cases, the preparation of SEM images has been limited to visual observation and comparison of two samples: control and treated or wild and mutant. However, the most important question that has not been clearly answered so far is how to process the images and extract quantitative information for statistical comparisons. In this protocol, for the first time, an attempt has been made to accurately answer this question by explaining, step by step, the processing and quantification of images obtained from SEM. This method measures different parts of the image according to their scale. The data obtained can be used for further analyses (Fig. 7 and 8).

steps.title: Soften dried rice stem tissue
steps.instruction: Immerse the thoroughly dried rice stem pieces in glycerol (a low‑vapor‑pressure liquid) to replace water and soften the silica‑rich tissue before sectioning.

steps.title: Trim paraffin‑embedded sample
steps.instruction: Trim the paraffin block containing the fixed rice stem tissue to expose a flat surface suitable for sectioning.

steps.title: Cut sections of desired thickness
steps.instruction: Section the trimmed tissue with a microtome; for optical microscopy aim for ~7 µm thickness, while for SEM any thickness that yields a smooth vertical face is acceptable.

steps.title: Prepare gelatin slides (or paraffin adhesive)
steps.instruction: Make gelatin‑coated microscope slides according to standard protocols (see Video 7) or alternatively melt paraffin on the slide to serve as an adhesive for the cut sections.

steps.title: Affix sections to slides
steps.instruction: Place each cut section onto the prepared gelatin (or paraffin‑coated) slide and gently press to ensure firm attachment.

steps.title: Dewax sections with toluene
steps.instruction: Immerse the slide‑mounted sections in toluene solvent to remove paraffin from the tissue, completing the dewaxing step required for SEM imaging.

steps.title: Image sections by SEM
steps.instruction: Load the dewaxed, slide‑mounted samples into the scanning electron microscope and acquire images under the desired imaging conditions.

steps.title: Quantify SEM images in ImageJ
steps.instruction: Open the SEM images in ImageJ, calibrate the scale, and measure the desired morphological features step‑by‑step as described in the protocol to obtain quantitative data for statistical analysis.
